channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan enhances cooperation with ICAO on civil aviation development
item.description: Uzbekistan is expanding its partnership with the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) to boost civil aviation. Discussions focused on ICAO's role in international aviation, its activities, and collaboration with Uzbekistan. The country aims to modernize airport infrastructure and improve services to enhance tourism.

item.title: Foreign investors show growing interest in Uzbekistan's fisheries sector
item.description: Foreign investment and loans in Uzbekistan's agriculture, forestry, and fisheries sectors are increasing significantly. In January-June 2026, the sector attracted 26 trillion soums in foreign capital, representing 10% of the republic's total. This marks a substantial rise from previous years, indicating growing investor confidence.

item.title: New engineering university 'ToshTech' opens in Uzbekistan with modern facilities
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev visited the new 'ToshTech' university, established to transform higher engineering education. The reconstructed seven-story building features modern laboratories and equipment. The university offers state grants, with 400 talented students admitted for the 2026/2027 academic year.

item.title: Russia Threatens Lithuania with Nuclear Weapons Use, Citing Direct Threat
item.description: Russia has threatened Lithuania with the use of nuclear weapons, with Dmitry Peskov stating that any weapons of mass destruction appearing on Lithuanian territory would pose a direct threat to Russia. Moscow warned it would take appropriate retaliatory measures in response to such a development.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Transport Clarifies Public Transport Fare Revision Discussions
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Transport has clarified that no final decision has been made regarding public transport fare revisions in Tashkent. A draft proposal suggests increasing single rides to 2500 soms via electronic payment, with cash fares at 3000 soms and baggage at 4000 soms. New subscription and transfer tariffs are also proposed.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Constitutional and Supreme Courts See Changes in Membership
item.description: Uzbekistan's Senate has approved changes to the composition of the Constitutional and Supreme Courts. Gairat Mashkurov was elected a judge of the Constitutional Court for 10 years, while K. Davletova was released from her post. Four new judges were elected to the Supreme Court, and several judges were released due to other work or personal requests.

item.title: Uzbek Senate Chair Emphasizes Practical Solutions and Concrete Results for All Issues
item.description: Tanzila Narbaeva, Chair of the Senate of Uzbekistan, stressed the need for practical solutions and concrete results on all issues raised. She stated that vague phrases like 'measures are being taken' are insufficient. Clear accountability, timelines, and expected outcomes are required, especially for budget-related matters.

item.title: Eurasian Development Bank Predicts 8.3% Economic Growth for Tajikistan This Year
item.description: The Eurasian Development Bank forecasts Tajikistan's economy to grow by 8.3% this year. The country is expected to maintain one of the highest growth rates among Central Asian nations.

item.title: Shavkat Mirziyoyev Visits Situational Center at Student Town in Almaty
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev visited the situational center at the student town in Almaty. The center monitors student safety, social environment in real-time, attendance, and crime prevention.

item.title: President Visits "Qichqiriq" Neighborhood, Sees New Park and Kindergarten
item.description: President visited the "Qichqiriq" neighborhood to observe its development. 71.4 billion soums were allocated for landscaping, resulting in a new park, sports grounds, and other facilities.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and UK Discuss Cooperation within UN Security Council
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ambassador to the UK, Omar Sultanov, met with Eleanor McEwan of the UK Foreign Ministry to discuss cooperation priorities and planned visits. Sultanov outlined Kyrgyzstan's priorities for its upcoming UN Security Council membership in 2027-2028, with the UK expressing readiness to engage.

item.title: Uzbek President Discusses Bilateral Cooperation with Armenian Prime Minister
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev held a phone call with Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan to discuss developing bilateral relations, focusing on trade, economy, and investment. They emphasized industrial cooperation and strengthening connectivity via transport corridors. The importance of a peace agreement for regional stability was also noted.

item.title: Uzbek President Meets Founder of Vietnam's ROX Group to Discuss Investment Projects
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with Anh Tuan Chan, founder of Vietnam's ROX Group, to discuss mutually beneficial cooperation and investment projects in Uzbekistan. Priority areas include urban and industrial infrastructure, renewable energy, geology, finance, and tourism. An agreement was reached to accelerate current and new projects.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Senate approves border changes between Kyzyryk and Jarqurghan districts
item.description: Uzbekistan's Senate approved changes to the borders of Kyzyryk and Jarqurghan districts. 4,740 hectares from Jarqurghan district will be transferred to Kyzyryk district, affecting 4,200 residents. This aims to improve access to state services and facilitate efficient land and water resource use.

item.title: Three Arrested in Sirdaryo After Environmental Inspector's Death
item.description: Three individuals have been detained in Sirdaryo on suspicion of causing the death of an environmental inspector, Mirzo Botirov, due to negligence. A criminal case has been initiated for violating wildlife protection, resisting authority, and negligent homicide.

item.title: Kazakh President Praises Kyrgyzstan's Organization of World Nomad Games
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev thanked Kyrgyzstan for organizing the VI World Nomad Games, stating they were held at a high level with fair results. He emphasized sports' role in fostering mutual respect and friendship among peoples.

item.title: Tokayev praises Nomad Games organization, thanks Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev thanked Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov for organizing the 6th World Nomad Games. Tokayev stated the games were held at a high level with fair results. He emphasized sports' role in fostering mutual respect and friendship between nations.

item.title: Tashkent Considers Raising Public Transport Fare to 2,500 UZS
item.description: Tashkent is considering increasing the public transport fare from the current 1,700 UZS to 2,500 UZS starting November 2023. The proposal is open for public discussion until September 19, considering the city's growing passenger volume and bus fleet.

item.title: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon Inaugurates Juice Production Subsidiary in Rasht Region
item.description: On September 11, Tajik President Emomali Rahmon commissioned a new juice production subsidiary in the Rasht region during his working visit. The enterprise aims to develop domestic production, process local raw materials, and increase import-substituting goods. It created 17 local jobs and has a production capacity of 540,000 liters per season.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan extends fuel price controls until end of 2026
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Antimonopoly Regulation Service has agreed to maintain capped prices for AI 92 gasoline, diesel, and autogas until the end of 2026. The government will compensate importers for the difference between production costs and consumer prices, with specific rates set for different regions.

item.title: New schools, medical centers, and language centers opened in Gissar for Independence Day
item.description: In Gissar, several new social facilities were launched in honor of the 35th anniversary of Tajikistan's independence. These include a language center, medical and dental clinics, and new educational buildings. The facilities are equipped with modern amenities and aim to improve education and healthcare.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan plans to resolve textbook deficit in schools by 2030
item.description: Kyrgyzstan aims to eliminate the shortage of textbooks in its schools by 2030. The publishing house 'Okuu Kitebi' has supplied millions of textbooks, with further millions planned for 2025-2026. New domestic textbooks for subjects like history and geography are also in development.

item.title: Uzbekistan increases meat imports amid market price concerns
item.description: Uzbekistan has increased its meat imports, according to customs data. This comes amid social media reports of halted imports and rising meat prices. The State Customs Committee stated there are no disruptions in imports. Market prices in Tashkent were investigated.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan prints 20 and 50-som banknotes domestically for the first time
item.description: For the first time since independence, Kyrgyzstan has printed 20 and 50-som banknotes domestically. The National Bank stated this initiative aims to strengthen economic independence. Previously, national currency was printed abroad for over 30 years. The bank did not specify production numbers or circulation dates.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan sets fuel prices until end of 2026, state to compensate importers
item.description: Kyrgyzstan will maintain capped prices for AI-92 gasoline, diesel, and autogas until the end of 2026. The Antimonopoly Service reached agreements with importers, with the state compensating the difference between import costs and consumer prices. Prices vary by region, with higher rates for remote mountainous areas.

item.title: Bishkek City Court sentences nephrologist Beishebaeva to three years in prison
item.description: The Bishkek City Court sentenced nephrologist Nasira Beishebaeva to three years in prison, overturning a previous house arrest order. Beishebaeva was detained after a patient's mother accused medical staff of negligence leading to the girl's leg amputation. Her lawyer stated the doctor tried her best to help the patient.

item.title: Uzbekistan integrates into the global market through economic reforms
item.description: Uzbekistan has transitioned from a closed, resource-based economy to an open model integrating into the global market. Reforms since 2017, including currency convertibility and tax liberalization, have attracted significant foreign investment into sectors like "green" energy, textiles, and pharmaceuticals. Foreign trade now spans over 160 countries, with key partners including China, Russia, Turkey, and South Korea.

item.title: Dushanbe to Host International Textile Forum 'Tajikistan - 2026'
item.description: The International Textile Forum 'Tajikistan - 2026' will be held in Dushanbe on September 23, 2026. The event aims to discuss the development of Tajikistan's textile industry, attract foreign investment, and showcase the sector's potential. The forum will also serve as a platform for investors interested in full-cycle textile projects.

item.title: Uzbekistan expands international cooperation with Sweden and Finland
item.description: Uzbekistan's First Deputy Senate Chairman met with the ambassadors of Sweden and Finland to discuss strengthening bilateral relations, inter-parliamentary cooperation, and trade-economic ties. Key areas for collaboration include education, digital technologies, ecology, water resource management, and think tank exchanges. Regular dialogue between parliamentary groups and cooperation within international organizations were agreed upon.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Implement Heritage Impact Assessment System for Historic Cities
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to implement a Heritage Impact Assessment (HIA) system to protect its unique historical cities like Bukhara, Samarkand, Khiva, Shakhrisabz, and Tashkent. The system aims to preserve historical monuments amidst infrastructure development. Digital platforms and monitoring tools will be utilized.

item.title: Maximum Fine for Noise Violations in Uzbekistan to Increase to 8.8 Million Som
item.description: In Uzbekistan, the maximum fine for exceeding noise level standards for vehicles will be increased to 8.8 million som. Drivers of vehicles exceeding noise limits will face a fine of 440,000 som without prior warning.

item.title: Uzbek National Guard officers to introduce themselves when interacting with citizens
item.description: Uzbekistan's Senate approved amendments to the law on the National Guard, requiring officers to introduce themselves when interacting with citizens. The changes aim to eliminate legal inconsistencies and fill practical gaps. The National Guard's primary tasks are being streamlined, and new duties include independently or jointly responding to public disorder and illegal actions.

item.title: Russian Interior Ministry reports 40% drop in migrant crime amid increased checks
item.description: Russia's Interior Ministry reports a 40% decrease in crimes committed by migrants. However, the number of checks increased by 155,000, with 43% more individuals screened.

item.title: Russian Interior Ministry reports 40% decrease in crimes by foreign citizens
item.description: Crimes by foreign citizens in Russia decreased by 40% in the first half of 2026, according to the Interior Ministry. This is attributed to expanded powers allowing focus on organized crime and illegal migration.

item.title: Uzbekistan's privatization drive creates new opportunities for private capital
item.description: Uzbekistan is implementing measures to reduce state ownership and expand the private sector, including a new privatization phase offering state assets. This initiative, particularly significant for the energy sector, aims to boost efficiency and attract private capital. A presidential decree outlines the sale of stakes in 84 companies, real estate, and land, valued at approximately 100 trillion soums.

item.title: South Korean President invites Central Asian leaders to Seoul for economic summit
item.description: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung has invited leaders from Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, and Turkmenistan to a summit in Seoul on September 16. The meeting will focus on deepening trade and economic cooperation.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan proposes stricter wartime measures including detention without ID
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering a draft constitutional law to significantly alter procedures during states of emergency and martial law. Proposals include expanding grounds for emergency declarations, deploying armed forces, and establishing a Security Council command body. Curfews, personal searches, and detention of individuals without identification for up to two days are also proposed.

item.title: WHO: 727,000 People Die by Suicide Annually Worldwide
item.description: The World Health Organization reports that approximately 727,000 people die by suicide globally each year. Suicide is the third leading cause of death for individuals aged 15-29. Low- and middle-income countries account for 73% of cases.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Reduce Exceptions for Underage Marriage
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to shorten the list of valid reasons for marriage before the legal age. The government also intends to strengthen accountability for promoting underage marriages. Currently, only two exceptional circumstances allow for such unions.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Inaugurates Renovated Manas Ordo Complex in Talas
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov announced that 1.4 billion soms from the state budget were spent on renovating the Manas Ordo national complex in Talas. The renovation aims to create a modern museum combining heritage and technology, including facilities for events and cultural preservation. This initiative is part of Kyrgyzstan's 35th independence anniversary celebrations.
